Definition: of Latin origin; happy; Phelix (i.e. Felix), a Roman:--Felix.
BiblicalUsage: Felix is the Roman governor before whom Paul stands for two years, and his name means happy. Paul reasons with him about righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, and Felix trembles, but he leaves Paul bound, hoping for a bribe. Festus finds Paul still in prison when he succeeds Felix, and asks Agrippa to help him make sense of the case.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Felix is the portrait of a man who trembled and did nothing: he heard the gospel, felt its weight, and chose the bribe over the truth. His story is on his profile; here the name alone warns me that trembling without turning is not repentance.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
